title: Proof-of-Delivery tokens and SLA reconciliation for SIEM connectors
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: External SIEM/webhook sinks (Splunk/Datadog/third-party collectors) intermittently drop or reorder audit events during transient downstream failures. Current router+forwarder retries reduce loss but provide limited proof to customers and limited reconciliation tooling for differences between what we believe was delivered and what the sink reports. This causes costly support escalations for enterprise customers with compliance requirements.

Goal: Design and implement a lightweight proof-of-delivery (PoD) mechanism and SLA reconciliation workflow for high-tier tenants that: 1) produces compact signed delivery receipts for batches we transmit to external sinks; 2) surfaces per-tenant delivery deltas in the Console; 3) improves retry policy to be backpressure-aware and tenant-tier cognizant; and 4) exposes replayable manifests and DLQ hooks for forensic replay and auditability.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement a full exactly-once protocol with sink-side acceptance guarantees. It focuses on verifiable delivery receipts, improved observability, reconciler tooling, and safer retry/backoff mechanics. A later follow-up may explore two-phase commit/handshake with selected enterprise SIEM partners.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Forwarder emits cryptographically signed PoD tokens for every successful HTTP 2xx fanout to a configured SIEM sink for P0/P1 tenants. 2) Console shows per-tenant delivered vs emitted counts with drift alerts when delta > 0.1% for 24h. 3) Reconciler job (daily) computes deltas and surfaces candidate missing ranges with links to replay manifest. 4) Retry policy honors target tenant's SLO and applies jittered exponential backoff with circuit-breaker for sustained 5xx/429 responses. 5) Integration test harness simulates Splunk/Datadog and demonstrates <0.01% undetected loss over 1M events with injected transient failures. 6) Security review signed-off and PoD keys rotated by KMS.
rollout_plan: Phase A (canary): enable PoD and reconciliation for 3 internal tenants and a single low-volume external tenant in staging. Phase B (pilot): enable for 10 P1 customers behind feature flag; collect metrics for 7 days. Phase C (gradual): enable for all P1 tenants and add opt-in for P2. If drift or performance regressions appear, automatic fallback to current best-effort delivery is triggered and PoD tokens are sampled instead of emitted for all traffic until resolved.
monitoring_queries:
Splunk query: index=audits sink=prod_siempool | stats count as emitted_count by tenant_id | lookup pod_tokens by tenant_id
Console metric names: audit.forwarder.pod_emitted_count, audit.forwarder.http_2xx_count, audit.forwarder.replay_requests, audit.forwarder.dlq_puts
Alert: audit.forwarder.drift_pct_last_24h > 0.1 for tenant tier in (P1,P0)
comments: 2026-03-04 - Asha Menon: Kicked off RFC (link in artifacts_links). Initial design proposes per-batch PoD tokens signed by KMS-backed key and embedded in delivery metadata. Requested review from Security and Platform infra.

2026-03-06 - Diego Morales: Prototype PoD token schema and signed envelope implemented on a local forwarder branch. Token contains sink_id, batch_id (monotonic per-tenant), emitted_count, first_seq, last_seq, timestamp, and signature. See PR draft: github PR link added.

2026-03-08 - Security review comment (Marina Kovacs): Approve concept but require explicit threat model for token leakage, KMS key access controls, and rotation window. Also recommend HMAC-subkey per-tenant to limit blast radius. Marked security_review_required=true.

2026-03-09 - Diego Morales: Adjusted key handling to use envelope encryption with per-tenant wrapped HMAC keys stored in KMS; added rotation script. Updated prototype and unit tests. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-forwarder/pull/738

2026-03-11 - QA: Integration harness simulating Splunk via local endpoint shows PoD emission adds median 3ms per-batch CPU cost and increases 95th p95 latency for small requests by ~7ms. Working with infra to micro-optimize signing path and offload to separate signing worker for high-throughput tenants.

2026-03-12 - Diego Morales: Implemented backpressure-aware retry: when remote responds 429 with Retry-After, forwarder slows batch emit and marks tenant queue as throttled; circuit-breaker trips after 30s of sustained 5xx/429, routes to DLQ and surfaces on Console. Added metrics and dashboard panel.

2026-03-14 - PM review (Lena Park): Pilot scope approved. Added acceptance criteria for reconciliation job and drift threshold. Schedule pilot cutover 2026-03-20. Added customer communications draft to Confluence.
